title: Zero Proof and ClawTails
lessons: The player sees White Claw Zero Proof and realizes the brand now offers a 0% alcohol product with familiar social styling.
The player already knows White Claw and sees ClawTails, a line built around recognizable cocktail flavor names.

text: Rooftop bar. Someone hands you a can. It looks exactly like a White Claw. It says Zero Proof on it.
A shared screen bolted to the rooftop bar loops a highlight reel: a logo dead center of the WrestleMania mat, both corners of an octagon rebranded into recovery zones.

entry-first-screen-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Is that PRIME? On the wrestling mat?

entry-first-screen-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Someone bought the middle of the ring and called it hydration. I bought a wave-shaped cardboard display. We are not the same kind of desperate.

entry-first-screen-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: You're just jealous you didn't think of it first.

entry-first-screen-4.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Absolutely not. Anyway. Look what I actually brought you up here for.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: A White Claw with no alcohol is a funny sentence.

entry-first-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: It still fits in the cooler.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: But I thought you were the fizzy alcohol one.

entry-first-4.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Zero Proof. Zero percent. Same can, same fizz, none of the other thing. Some nights the can's the point and the alcohol isn't. I finally noticed.

choice-first.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: You've been holding it for a minute. Open it or hand it back, no judgment.

choices.text: I like having the same kind of drink without alcohol.
I'm not sure I need White Claw branding if there's no alcohol.

first-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Then the can still means something without the alcohol. I wasn't sure it would. That's a relief, honestly.

first-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Fair. Without the alcohol, you're deciding if you still want me. Just me. That's a weird thing to find out on a roof.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That sounds like a branding case study.

first-2-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Please never say that at the beach.

first-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Sparkling water remains extremely difficult to beat on simplicity.
Same rooftop, different night. The cooler has cans you haven't seen before. The names on them belong to cocktails.

entry-return-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Margarita. Cosmo. Mojito. Daiquiri.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You stole the cocktail menu.

entry-return-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Borrowed the names. Very different legal energy.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: And the can is not pretending to be the actual cocktail?

entry-return-5.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Cocktail-inspired. You know what a margarita is, so you know roughly what the can is. That's all the name's doing. It's doing a lot.

choice-return.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Pick one. I'll tell you which one's actually good after.

choices.text: That sounds fun for a rooftop hang.
Cocktail names are setting a lot of expectations.
I'd rather have the actual cocktail or the regular seltzer.

return-1.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Good. That's the whole idea. You already know how to want a margarita. I just put it in a can and skipped the blender.

return-2.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Yeah. The name sells it before you taste it. Sometimes the taste keeps up. Sometimes you get a mojito that tastes like a very confident lime.

return-3.speaker: WHITE CLAW
text: Then this one didn't fix anything for you. That's fine. The regular cans are under it.
